usage: The phrase 'faan1 gung1' is commonly used to indicate the action of going to one’s workplace.
It can be used in casual and formal contexts when discussing daily work routines.
'Faan1 gung1' literally means 'return to work,' but it also broadly applies to starting work or heading to a job.
This expression does not specify the type of work, so it can be used for any professional or manual job.
It is often paired with time expressions to talk about when one starts or finishes work.

examples.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1zou2 cat1 dim2 zau6 jiu3 faan1 gung1.
examples.meaning: I have to go to work at 7 in the morning.

examples.sentence: 聽日星期六我唔返工，可以休息。
examples.jyutping: ting1 jat6 sing1 kei4 luk6 ngo5 m4 faan1 gung1, ho2 ji5 jau1 sik1.
examples.meaning: I don’t have to go to work tomorrow, I can rest.

examples.sentence: 返工前記得攞晒你嘅文件。
examples.jyutping: faan1 gung1 cin4 gei3 dak1 lo2 saai3 nei5 ge3 man4 gin2.
examples.meaning: Remember to take all your documents before going to work.

examples.sentence: 我今日好忙，一早就返工冇時間吹水。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 hou2 mong4, jat1 zou2 zau6 faan1 gung1 mou5 si4 gaan3 ceoi1 seoi2.
examples.meaning: I am very busy today and went to work early without time to chat.

related: 去上班 (heoi3 soeng5 baan1) - go to work
